subject: Throttling config translation error causing intermittent 429s — next steps
messages:
From: Simon Liu <simon.liu@novaco.com>

Subject: Sudden 429 spikes during bulk embed job (samples attached)

Hi Karthik / Redwood support,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses from the embeddings endpoint while running our nightly bulk ingest. The job has run reliably for months and started failing around 08:30 PDT this morning. Attached a small sample of request IDs and response headers (novaco-rate-sample-20270411.jsonl).

Impact: our downstream indexing pipeline is backlogged and we have customers hitting search errors. We're throttling the job manually but need this fixed ASAP.

Can you confirm whether this is a tenant-side limit, a job-level rate cap, or something on Redwood's side?

Simon

Karthik / Simon / Marissa — initial findings from the infra side: we correlated Simon's example request IDs against the rate-limiter logs and config generator traces. Root cause (short): a translation bug in the rate-config generator created an incorrect token-per-second mapping for Novaco's dedicated tenant profile during a nightly config rollout.

Details:
- At ~08:21 PDT a config push changed the per-tenant policy template. A translation function mistakenly interpreted a percentile bucket as an absolute tokens/sec value (off by a factor of ~10).
- The runtime enforced the lower tokens/sec value, which caused legitimate traffic bursts to be throttled (429).
- This only affected tenants that use the dedicated "burst-aware" profile — Novaco matches that criteria.

Immediate mitigation steps we've applied (10:00 PDT):
1) Rollback the last config change for Novaco's tenant to the prior template.
2) Temporarily bumped their tokens/sec soft cap by 3x on the runtime layer to give breathing room while we patch the generator.
3) Added a short-circuit guard in the rate-limiter to accept in-flight KV cache items for 5min during config rollouts to avoid transient under-enforcement.

Please validate on your side whether the nightly job can be re-run at reduced concurrency for a smoke test. We will keep the temporary bump in place until permanent fix is deployed.

I'll follow up with the patch and the code diff.

Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Simon — quick status update:

- Permanent patch to the rate-config generator deployed at 09:45 PDT 2027-04-12. The patch removes the incorrect percentile->absolute translation and adds unit tests + an integration test that replays the Novaco sample.
- We ran a canary across the dedicated-profile fleet from 09:50–09:58 PDT; no regressions observed.
- We rolled back the temporary tokens/sec bump at 09:59 PDT and validated no 429s for the sample request IDs you provided.

Next steps:
1) CS (Marissa) will send a proposed goodwill credit for the 2-hour impacted window.
2) SRE (Sean) will publish a technical postmortem (internal+customer-friendly) at the link below within 72 hours.
3) We will add a gating check to the config pipeline so a translation discrepancy >2x will fail the rollout.

Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/NVC-20270411
